points: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has sanctioned an additional 25 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) for deployment during the Urban Local Body (ULB) elections in Tripura slated for November 27.

items.title: ASIA LNG MOC PERFORMANCE: Deliveries conclude for record volume of 148.5 TBtu during August MOC
points: Participants in the Asia LNG Platts Market on Close assessment process concluded physical deliveries for a record volume of 148.5 TBtu during August, according to operational trade performance data compiled by Platts, part of S&P Global Energy.
The milestone topples the last high recorded just a month ago, when 34 trades – amounting to 113 TBtu – were concluded for LNG product traded in July.
Over the past 10 months of this year, LNG traded volumes have already risen to record highs three times, the first being in January when MOC activity saw 110 TBtu changing hands, Platts data showed.
There were 44 trades in total during the August MOC, with volumes rising 29.03% month over month and 61.82% year over year.
Shell was the biggest buyer with 82.9 TBtu, while QaterEnergy Trading was the largest seller with 43.3 TBtu, Platts data showed.
Participants attributed the rise in MOC activity in part to a persistently closed East-West arbitrage, which limited the flow of marginal US-sourced cargoes into the region.

The accident occurred on November 19 at Amazon Plywoods in Vettikkattukunnu, Mudickal, near Perumbavoor.
The victim was the four-year-old son of Jamal, a migrant worker from Assam.
According to initial reports, Jamal and his family had arrived at the factory for work on the day of the accident.

items.title: Opinion: Opinion | Blinded By Decree: Why Suspending BARC Ratings Paralyses Indian Television
points: By severing the single thread of empirical currency that holds India's television market together, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's (MIB) suspension of the Broadcast Audience Research Council (BARC) ratings is an act of policy self-sabotage.
Intended as a regulatory pause or a pressure tactic to accelerate compliance under the Television Ratings Policy, 2026, the blackout has instead triggered an immediate commercial paralysis.
In attempting to cure a perceived institutional ailment, the government has chosen to suffocate the patient.
Television advertising relies entirely on third-party verification to price inventory, establish reach, and deliver return on investment (ROI).

Linear television, already grappling with structural declines, regulatory friction, and ad-revenue erosion, cannot afford an artificial drought that permanently redirects Indian brand spending into foreign tech giants.
This is a catastrophic miscalculation considering that an estimated 70% of television channels are free-to-air and rely solely on ad-sales to survive.
Suspending an entire measurement currency paralyses commercial predictability while doing nothing to solve the methodological disputes at hand.

items.title: US Navy Supply Ship USNS Wally Schirra Arrives In India For 5th Repair Visit To L&T Yard
points: USNS Wally Schirra of the U.S. Navy has arrived at the Kattupalli shipyard of Larsen & Toubro (L&T) near Chennai in southern India for repairs.
The supply ship reached the yard on November 20 under the India-US Master Ship Repair Agreement (MSRA), India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.
USNS Wally Schirra is also the first U.S. naval ship to reach the yard for repairs since India brought a revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for the entry and exit of ship crews into force.
Ship-repair cooperation between India and the U.S. began in August 2022 when USNS Charles Drew became the first U.S. Navy ship to be repaired at an Indian shipyard.
The Kattupalli yard later carried out repairs on USNS Matthew Perry in March 2023 and USNS Salvor in July 2023 before USNS Charles Drew returned in December 2024.
L&T signed the MSRA with the U.S. Navy in April 2023, which allows the Kattupalli yard to take up voyage repairs of American naval vessels.

items.title: Strait Of Hormuz Traffic Stays 65% Below Pre-War Levels As 6 Tankers Are Attacked In A Week
points: Strait of Hormuz shipping stayed about 65% below pre-conflict levels in mid-November as six tankers came under attack in the region.

The weekly overview counted 263 vessel transits through the strategic waterway in the seven days to November 18, down from 308 in the previous week.
Vessels broadcasting their Automated Identification System (AIS) positions accounted for 73 of these transits, down from 82 the previous week.
UKMTO reported attacks on six tankers during the week, with four in the Strait of Hormuz and two in the Persian Gulf.
On November 17, a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile about 13 nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman while sailing out of the strait.
UKMTO has recorded 106 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began on February 28, 2026.

items.title: Supreme Court Clears Karnataka Bike Taxis: What Changes For Ola, Uber And Rapido?
points: Bike taxi operators in Karnataka have received major relief after the Supreme Court dismissed the state government’s appeal against a High Court ruling that allowed motorcycles to be used for paid passenger rides.
The decision, delivered on 20 November 2026, removes a major legal obstacle for companies such as Rapido, Uber and Ola.
They can now seek registration and permits for bike taxi operations, with conditions that transport authorities can impose under the Motor Vehicles Act.
In April 2025, a single judge of the Karnataka High Court ordered operators to stop their services until the state put the required rules in place.
On 20 November, a bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh dismissed the state’s challenge, leaving the High Court decision in force.
A motorcycle registered for private use does not become a licensed taxi simply because the Supreme Court dismissed Karnataka’s appeal.
The Centre’s Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, say that state governments may allow app-based passenger rides on non-transport motorcycles.
